name: google-workspace-mcp
description: Google Workspace MCP server — Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets via HTTP transport

native_build._comment: type image-wrapper (2026-07-03): type 'app' made the Dockerfile generator treat the whole entrypoint string as a binary to COPY — the image shipped with NO uv and no app code, dying with 'exec uv failed'. image-wrapper is the working sibling pattern (google-personal-mcp). base_image = official uv+python image so `uv sync`/`uv run` exist. entrypoint uses `uv run --no-sync` (2026-09-30): plain `uv run` re-synced the venv (dev group incl. ruff) at every start; deps are baked by `cmd` at build. Guarded by src/test-startup-contract.mjs.

drain._doc: #1659: this container runs work that lasts hours (an unzip-to-Drive job is a thread of the server; the 2026-11-11 Takeout and repository backups were scripts run with docker exec) and a recreate SIGKILLs all of it. With drain declared the ship engine (cloud-ship-container-step-deploy-drain.sh) pipes the probe into the container first: nothing live -> recreates now; something live -> names it in the ship log, leaves the recreate to the waiter on the VM and the old container keeps serving until the work ends. While a recreate waits, start_drive_unzip refuses new jobs (the probe's hold). After max_wait_seconds the recreate runs over whatever is still live and names it. Operator override: SHIP_DRAIN_FORCE=1.

resources._comment: #1659: THE ONE DECLARATION of this container's memory budget (compose.nix reads it). Reviewed after the 2026-11-11 OOM kill (exit 137 on a 417 MB download): the ceiling was not the defect, the tool held ~4 copies of the file in memory. Every Drive transfer now streams through disk in chunks of at most 16 MiB (core/streaming.py), heavy calls are limited to 2 at a time and an unzip job to 4 upload threads, so the working set is the Python baseline plus tens of MiB. 2G stays as the ceiling (same as the app-category default, so no new resource is reserved or paid for) and 256M is declared as the reservation the kernel protects under host pressure, like the sibling MCPs. GET /health reports the live headroom.

mcp.description: Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Forms, Slides, Chat, Tasks, Contacts, Search, Apps Script via OAuth 2.0/2.1.

stability._comment: #1659: Drive transfers stream through disk in bounded chunks (never a whole file in memory), expired attachments are removed, the unzip-to-Drive job runs against a fake Drive backend, and the unzip methods are listed in the grouped workspace_drive tool. Standard library only: no Google packages needed on the runner. The tool-level tests with a mocked Drive service (code/tests/gdrive/test_drive_streaming_tools.py) need the project venv and run with pytest.

runtime._why_oom_score_adj: #1659: every MCP server on oci-apps is in the last tier the kernel OOM killer picks (_shared/oom-priority.json, tier mcp). Restart policy is 'no' (owner rule), so a killed MCP stays down and its tools are gone until someone starts it by hand. -900 = the host's connectivity tier; not -1000, which would also exempt it from its own cgroup limit.
